question: On the actual PR49 endpoints, does a smaller late-stage Adam step improve joint E1/E2/F1/F2/E3 retention and convergence under equal new exposure?
start: All three actual PR49 final-after-TF complete states; never an earlier best checkpoint
preserved: cap32 own-prefix greedy generation with external S
paired_course: Continue seed+666000 RNG after the nine E3 epochs already taught; generate and publish the next four exact 53100-target permutations. Pair both arms by identical permutation bytes.
budget_note: Equal to PR49's total new optimizer updates, now split over two paired policies. Excludes inference and I/O. Not a runtime estimate.
fixed_budget: All arms end after the fourth new epoch. Record earlier milestones but do not select or restore earlier checkpoints; no adaptive extra epochs or extra learning-rate sweep.
baseline: Validate each of the three parents once against its archived 4500-question generation; abort before any optimizer update on a mismatch. Do not duplicate physical baseline cost for the two branches.
metrics: mean total errors over the last two epochs
mean old-four-class errors over the last two epochs
historical_gate: Keep the original all-five-classes 900/900 for two consecutive new epochs milestone unchanged. Final-two-epoch stability is an additional endpoint metric, not a retroactive replacement of historical gates.
local_policy_support_rule: The smaller-step arm must be no worse for both last-two mean total errors and last-two mean old-class errors in every paired seed, with at least one strict total-error improvement. Report ties and each seed; this is a local descriptive policy comparison, not a universal learning-rate claim.
limits: No heldout scores used for stopping or selection
No claim that fixed-bank convergence proves general copy
decision_dependency: Use this candidate if the near-term priority is consolidating the existing five-task bank. If the priority is new-combination generalization, design a separate curriculum/heldout study informed by the frozen-weight E3 probe; do not silently combine both changes.
